registry:hook/use-mobile.reason: Native window dimensions replace matchMedia; tested at the breakpoint, on resize and on subscription cleanup. Device acceptance remains separate.

registry:hook/use-highlighted-code.reason: Native Text output, thirteen grammars, aliases, ANSI, grammar state, streaming updates and theme switching tested. Hermes/device acceptance remains pending.

registry:ui/form.reason: React Hook Form provider/controller, required errors, native input binding and submission tested. Upstream form examples, resolver integrations and focus/accessibility acceptance remain pending.

webSpecific.feature: HTML tags, DOM refs and browser events
webSpecific.adaptation: Replace with typed React Native host components, native refs and event payloads. A name-only or HTML-backed adapter is not an Expo port.

webSpecific.feature: CSS styles, selectors, hover and focus-visible
webSpecific.adaptation: Preserve each style's design intent with shared-token native StyleSheets, pressed/focus state and responsive layout; document selectors with no native meaning.

webSpecific.feature: Next routes, Server Components, server actions and HTML form actions
webSpecific.adaptation: Use explicit application navigation and native submit callbacks; keep authentication and persistence in the application's existing API. Do not ship working-looking provider stubs.
Use native SVG with each example's series, scale, axes, stacking, labels and interactions accounted for. Six generic chart renderers do not establish chart-registry parity.

webSpecific.feature: window.matchMedia, innerWidth and DOM resize observers
webSpecific.adaptation: Use subscribed native window dimensions and native layout events, including rotation, split-screen and cleanup.

webSpecific.feature: Browser clipboard, storage, file input and drag/drop
webSpecific.adaptation: Use Expo/native platform bridges, explicit permission/error handling and touch/accessible alternatives. Do not execute browser APIs on device.

webSpecific.feature: next/font, CSS font variables and web font providers
webSpecific.adaptation: Track every font and weight; native font loading requires actual Expo-compatible font assets and family mapping. CSS font metadata alone is not a native font port.

webSpecific.feature: Shiki HTML spans and CSS theme variables
webSpecific.adaptation: Keep grammar/state behavior using the JavaScript regex engine, but render themed native Text rather than HTML.
